answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols utilize economic staking to enforce Sybil resistance, requiring agents to commit capital to validate network states. An attacker must acquire a massive stake, akin to moving a frozen glacier of capital, to gain control. This validation process functions like a high-density orchard of trust where malicious actors face slashing, a penalty that turns their assets into ferrous scrap metal by stripping them of value. The cost remains prohibitively high as increasing validator counts mandates exponential liquidity.
